name: Refugee Status (Refugees and Asylum Seekers Law 2023)

requirements.blocker_text: Must submit a formal application to the Refugee Status Determination Committee; any person within Somalia's territory may apply, and the Committee must provide an opportunity to be heard (with interpreters where needed) and an appeal right before a final decision.
requirements.fix_path: Submit an application to the Refugee Status Determination Committee.

evidence_required.document: Testimony/interview before the Refugee Status Determination Committee

outcome.duration_length: not specified precisely in the source located in this build

sources.title: UNHCR Rights Mapping and Analysis Platform (RIMAP) -- Somalia's Refugees and Asylum Seekers Law (2023): a comprehensive domestic refugee-protection framework covering the right to enter and seek asylum, non-refoulement, non-discrimination (age, race, gender, disability, political opinion), immunity from unlawful-presence prosecution for applicants and their families while a claim is pending, special safeguards for women/unaccompanied children/elderly/disabled applicants, and rights to work, education, health, housing, freedom of movement, documentation, and family life for recognized refugees; applications go to a Refugee Status Determination Committee with a right to be heard, interpretation, and appeal

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Somalia). STATUS: DRAFT -- tier-2 UNHCR-hosted summary only; no tier-1 Somali-government-hosted copy of the 2023 Law or its implementing Refugee Status Determination Committee regulations was located (a National Commission for Refugees and IDPs, NCRI Somalia, appears to exist and administer this area, but its own portal/gazette text was not independently retrieved in this build). GENUINELY POSITIVE STRUCTURAL FINDING, WORTH STATING PLAINLY: unlike Bangladesh and Pakistan (both built earlier in this dataset with NO domestic asylum law at all, relying instead on colonial-era discretionary-exemption statutes or UNHCR mandate-only processing), Somalia has enacted its own comprehensive, named, rights-detailed refugee law as recently as 2023 -- a genuinely modern domestic framework on paper, rare among the harder-context countries built in this dataset. THE OBVIOUS TENSION, STATED PLAINLY: Somalia enacting a modern refugee-protection law for INBOUND asylum seekers sits alongside Somalia being one of the world's largest REFUGEE- AND IDP-PRODUCING countries itself (decades of conflict, Al-Shabaab insurgency, recurring drought/famine, millions of Somalis displaced internally or living as refugees in Kenya, Ethiopia, Yemen, and elsewhere) -- this dataset models the inbound legal framework as enacted; it does not assess how many people actually use it, how consistently the Committee operates across contested territory, or the vastly larger reality of Somalis themselves seeking protection abroad. work_rights/study_rights set conservatively to 'restricted' since the source describes a right TO work/education in principle without detailing scope or limitations -- following this dataset's standard conservative default for thin humanitarian sourcing, unlike the deliberate 'full' departure made for Uganda's refugee law earlier in this dataset, since Somalia lacks Uganda's kind of independent tier-1 operational corroboration.
